newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court ruling on Islamist mayor sparks protest.
newsitem.headline: Turk court ruling on Islamist mayor sparks protest.

text.p: A Turkish court erupted in protest on Friday after a judge refused to release from custody a mayor from the ruling Islam-based Welfare Party facing charges of Islamist activism, state-run Anatolian news agency said.

People in the courtroom chanted "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest) and protesters scuffled with journalists after the judge announced the mayor and five other defendants would not be released from custody pending a verdict.
Anatolian quoted the judge as saying the protests were sparked by a defence lawyer's comment casting doubt on the neutrality of the court.
Bekir Yildiz, mayor of Ankara district Sincan, and 10 other people went on trial in April for organising an anti-Israel protest in Sincan, outraging the country's secularists.
Yildiz was charged with "aiding an armed gang and making its propaganda" and "provoking animosity among people".
He faces six to twelve years in jail if found guilty, the agency said. The other defendants face similar charges but four of them were allowed to leave jail after April's hearing.
At the anti-Israel evening, Yildiz and Iranian ambassador Ali Reza Bagheri spoke on a stage draped with a banner of the late leader of the militant Palestinian group Islamic Jihad Fathi Shqaqi.
Welfare leader Necmettin Erbakan, under pressure from the strictly secularist army, has toned down his pro-Islamist rhetoric since becoming prime minister last June.
He said last weekend he was seeking early elections to resolve a row between Welfare and the country's secular establishment. A date has not yet been set for the early polls.
